{{Short description|Norwegian mathematician (1924–1990)}}
'''Karl Egil Aubert''' (19 August 1924 &ndash; 21 October 1990) was a Norwegian mathematician.<ref name=snl>{{Store norske leksikon|Karl_Egil_Aubert}}</ref>

Karl  Aubert was born in [[Oslo|Christiania]] (now Oslo), Norway. He was the brother of sociologist [[Vilhelm Aubert]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=   https://nbl.snl.no/Vilhelm_Aubert|title=     Vilhelm Aubert|publisher =   Norsk biografisk leksikon |author=  Ragnvald Kalleberg|accessdate= January 1, 2017 }}</ref>

He studied at the [[University of Oslo]] and took his [[Doctor of Science]] degree at the [[University of Paris]]  in 1957. He  stayed at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] from 1958 to 1960. From 1962 to 1990 he was a professor at the [[University of Oslo]].   He was also a visiting professor at the [[University of Washington in Seattle]] and [[Tufts University]]. He chaired the [[Norwegian Mathematics Society]] from 1960 to 1967.
<ref>{{cite web|url=   https://nbl.snl.no/Karl_Egil_Aubert|title=     Karl Egil Aubert|publisher =   Norsk biografisk leksikon |author=  Erik Alfsen 
|accessdate= January 1, 2017 }}</ref>
